paragraphs: Gimlet is hosted software for keeping track of what happens at a service desk. It is sold to libraries and other organizations that want to see the trends and patterns behind the questions their desks field.

Staff log each interaction on a form the organization configures with its own category values. Entries can be tagged, and the full text of a question and its answer is kept so it can be searched later. A search can cover every entry or narrow to a single building or desk. Reports can show which desks are busiest at which hours of the week and which staff field the hardest questions. Data can be moved out to spreadsheet or reporting tools such as Excel, Google Sheets or Tableau. A web browser is all a desk needs to use it, and there is no cap on the number of staff or computers on an account.

Gimlet was founded by Eric Larson, a librarian, and Nate Vack, a library web application developer. The site puts the running total at more than 106,929,217 questions answered. The service is monitored around the clock for uptime, performance and security, with data mirrored, encrypted and backed up. Customers keep ownership of the data they enter. A 30-day free trial is offered.

quote.text: Turn your organization’s answers into insights easily.
